A flat owner can apply for HDB to buy back their flat if they face genuine difficulties selling their flat at a reasonable price due to one or more Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) limits, provided they have made regular, genuine attempts over a continuous period to market the flat (https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy).

To qualify for buyback assistance, flat owners must meet the following conditions:

* **EIP Constraint & Seller Background:** The flat owner must be constrained by one or more EIP limits and face genuine difficulties selling the flat at a reasonable price, regardless of whether the flat was originally bought directly from HDB or on the resale market (https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy).
* **Continuous Marketing Attempts:** The owner must have made regular genuine attempts over a continuous period to sell the flat (https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy). HDB currently considers six months of marketing to be sufficient for most owners, though this period may change based on prevailing market conditions (https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy).
* **Reasonable Asking Price:** The asking price must be set reasonably by referencing recent transaction prices for flats within 200m (using HDB's Transactions Within 200 Metres e-Service) and adjusting for flat attributes such as storey height and orientation (https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy).
* **Documentation/Records:** Owners must maintain and submit monthly records of their marketing attempts (e.g., online/print listings showing asking prices and listing dates, records of flat viewings) to HDB (https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy).

Flat owners who do not fulfill these criteria but face extenuating circumstances may seek special consideration from HDB (https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy).

A flat owner can apply for the HDB EIP Buyback Assistance Scheme if they are constrained by one or more Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) limits and have made regular, genuine attempts to sell the flat at a reasonable asking price over a continuous period, which HDB currently assesses as six months.

To be eligible, the flat owner must meet the following specific conditions:

*   **Genuine Marketing Efforts:** The owner must have made regular and genuine attempts to sell the flat while constrained by EIP limits. HDB assesses eligibility by comparing the marketing period to the time typically taken by most flat owners to sell, noting that six months is presently sufficient, though this may change with market conditions [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].
*   **Reasonable Asking Price:** The asking price must be reasonable. Owners are advised to reference recent transaction prices for flats within 200 meters of their property, adjusting for attributes like storey height and orientation, using data from HDB’s Transactions Within 200 Metres e-Service [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].
*   **Documentation:** Owners must keep and submit monthly records of their marketing attempts, such as online or print property listings (including asking price and listing date) and records of flat viewings [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].
*   **Eligible Flat Owners:** The scheme applies to flat owners who bought their flats from HDB or on the resale market, regardless of whether the flat was EIP-constrained at the time of purchase [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].

If a flat owner does not strictly fulfill these criteria but faces extenuating circumstances, they may seek special consideration from HDB [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy]. If HDB makes a buyback offer, the owner has up to three months to decide; if they decline, they are ineligible for buyback assistance for 12 months after the offer lapses [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].

- The period over which a flat owner has marketed the flat must be comparable to the time taken by most flat owners to sell their flats, which HDB presently considers to be six months based on its experience, though this may change depending on prevailing market conditions ([https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy)).
- To set a reasonable asking price, flat owners can take reference from recent transaction prices for flats located within 200m of their flat and make adjustments for attributes such as storey height and orientation, using details published via HDB's Transactions Within 200 Metres e-Service ([https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy)).
- Flat owners should keep monthly records of their marketing attempts throughout the marketing period (such as online or print property listings including asking price and listing date, and records of flat viewings) to submit to HDB when seeking assistance ([https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy)).
- EIP-constrained flat owners who do not fulfil these criteria but face extenuating circumstances may seek special consideration from HDB ([https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy)).
- Eligible flat owners include both those who bought their flats from HDB and those who purchased their flats on the resale market, regardless of whether the flat was EIP-constrained when it was bought ([https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy)).
